Let $A=\{x\in R:[x+3]+[x+4]\leq 3\},$

$B=\left \{x\in R:3^{x}\left (\sum\limits _{r=1}^{\infty }\frac{3}{10^{r}}\right )^{x-3}<3^{-3x}\right \},$ where [t] denotes greatest integer function. Then,
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We have,

$\begin{array}{l} A=\{x\in R:[x+3]+[x+4]\leq 3\} \\  \\ \text{Here,}[x+3]+[x+4]\leq 3 \\  \\ \Rightarrow [x]+3+[x]+4\leq 3 \\  \\ (\because [x+n]=[x]+n,n\in I) \\  \\ \Rightarrow 2[x]+4\leq 0\Rightarrow [x]\leq -2 \\  \\ \Rightarrow x\in (-\infty ,-1) \\  \\ A\equiv (-\infty ,-1)...........(i) \end{array}$

Also,

$B=\left \{x\in R:3^{x}\left (\sum\limits _{r=1}^{\infty }\frac{3}{10^{r}}\right )^{x-3}<3^{-3x}\right \}$

Here,

$\begin{array}{ll} \quad 3^{x}\left (\dfrac{3}{10}+\dfrac{3}{10^{2}}+\dfrac{3}{10^{3}}+\ldots \right )^{x-3}<3^{-3x} \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & 3^{x}\left (\dfrac{\frac{3}{10}}{1-\frac{1}{10}}\right )^{x-3}<3^{-3x} \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & 3^{x}\left (\dfrac{1}{3}\right )^{x-3}<3^{-3x} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow  & 3^{x-x+3}<3^{-3x}\Rightarrow 3^{3}<3^{-3x} \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & -3x>3\Rightarrow x<-1 \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & x\in (-\infty ,-1) \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & B\equiv (-\infty ,-1)...........(ii) \end{array}$

From equations (i) and (ii), we get

$A=B$

text:
If the system of equations

$x+y+az=b$

$2x+5y+2z=6$

$x+2y+3z=3$

has infinitely many solutions, then $2a+3b$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given system of equations,

$\text{and}\begin{array}{ll} x+y+az & =b \\ 2x+5y+2z & =6 \\ x+2y+3z & =3 \end{array}$

Since, given system of equation has infinitely many solutions

$\therefore D=0\text{and}D_{1}=D_{2}=D_{3}=0$

$\begin{array}{lllllll} \text{Here,}D=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & a \\ 2 & 5 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \end{array}\right |=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 1(15-4)-1(6-2)+a(4-5)=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow -a+11-4=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow a=7 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{lllllll} \text{and}D_{1}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} b & 1 & a \\ 6 & 5 & 2 \\ 3 & 2 & 3 \end{array}\right |=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow b(15-4)-1(18-6)+a(12-15)=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 11b-12-3a=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 11b-12-21=0(\because a=7) \\  \\ \Rightarrow 11b-33=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow b=3 \\  \\ \therefore 2a+3b=2(7)+3(3)=14+9=23 \end{array}$

text: The straight lines $\mathrm{l}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{l}_{2}$ pass through the origin and trisect the line segment of the line L : $9x+5y=45$ between the axes. If $\mathrm{m}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{m}_{2}$ are the slopes of the lines $\mathrm{l}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{l}_{2}$, then the point of intersection of the line $\mathrm{y}=(\mathrm{m}_{1}+\mathrm{m}_{2})x$ with L lies on :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
Given line $L:9x+5y=45$ ..........(i)


[IMG]


Also given that $m_{1}$ and $m_{2}$ are the slopes of the lines $l_{1}$ and $l_{2}$, respectively.

Let $A$ be the point of intersection of line $l_{1}$ and $L$, then 

co-ordinates of $A$ are $\left (\frac{2\times 5+1\times 0}{2+1},\frac{2\times 0+1\times 9}{2+1}\right )=\left (\frac{10}{3},3\right )$

And let $B$ be the point of intersection of line $l_{2}$ and $L$, then 

co-ordinates of $B$ are $\left (\frac{1\times 5+2\times 0}{1+2},\frac{1\times 0+2\times 9}{1+2}\right )=\left (\frac{5}{3},6\right )$

Now, slope of line $l_{1},(m_{1})=\frac{3-0}{\frac{10}{3}-0}=\frac{9}{10}$

and slope of lines $l_{2},(m_{2})=\frac{6-0}{\frac{5}{3}-0}=\frac{18}{5}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \therefore \text{line}y & =(m_{1}+m_{2})x \\  \\ =\left (\dfrac{9}{10}+\dfrac{18}{5}\right )x=\dfrac{45}{10}x=\dfrac{9}{2}x.......(ii) \end{array}$

Point of intersection of lines (i) and (ii)

$\begin{array}{l} 9x+5\left (\dfrac{9}{2}x\right )=45 \\  \\ \Rightarrow x+\dfrac{5x}{2}=5 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{7x}{2}=5\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{10}{7} \\  \\ \text{and}y=\dfrac{9}{2}\times \dfrac{10}{7}=\dfrac{45}{7} \\  \\ \therefore \text{Point of intersection}=\left (\dfrac{10}{7},\dfrac{45}{7}\right ) \\  \\ \text{lies on line}y-x=5 \end{array}$

text: One vertex of a rectangular parallelopiped is at the origin $\mathrm{O}$ and the lengths of its edges along $x,y$ and $z$ axes are $3,4$ and $5$ units respectively. Let $\mathrm{P}$ be the vertex $(3,4,5)$. Then the shortest distance between the diagonal OP and an edge parallel to $\mathrm{z}$ axis, not passing through $\mathrm{O}$ or $\mathrm{P}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Equation of $OP$ is

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{x-0}{3-0}=\dfrac{y-0}{4-0}=\dfrac{z-0}{5-0} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{x}{3}=\dfrac{y}{4}=\dfrac{z}{5} \end{array}$

Equation of edge parallel to $Z$-axis is

$\frac{x-3}{0}=\frac{y-0}{0}=\frac{z-5}{1}$

$\therefore$ Shortest distance

$=\frac{\left |\begin{array}{lll} x_{2}-x_{1} & y_{2}-y_{1} & z_{2}-z_{1} \\ a_{1} & b_{1} & c_{1} \\ a_{2} & b_{2} & c_{2} \end{array}\right |}{\sqrt{\begin{array}{l} (a_{1}b_{2}-a_{2}b_{1})^{2}+(b_{1}c_{2}-b_{2}c_{1})^{2}+(c_{1}a_{2}-c_{2}a_{1})^{2} \end{array}}}$

Here,

$\begin{array}{l} x_{1}=0,y_{1}=0,z_{1}=0 \\  \\ x_{2}=3,y_{2}=0,z_{2}=5 \\  \\ a_{1}=3,b_{1}=4,c_{1}=5 \\  \\ a_{2}=0,b_{2}=0,c_{2}=1 \end{array}$

$\therefore \left |\begin{array}{lll} x_{2}-x_{1} & y_{2}-y_{1} & z_{2}-z_{1} \\ a_{1} & b_{1} & c_{1} \\ a_{2} & b_{2} & c_{2} \end{array}\right |=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 3 & 0 & 5 \\ 3 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right |=4(3)=12$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{and}\sqrt{(a_{1}b_{2}-a_{2}b_{1})^{2}+(b_{1}c_{2}-b_{2}c_{1})^{2}+(c_{1}a_{2}-c_{2}a_{1})^{2}} \\  \\ =\sqrt{0+(4-0)^{2}+(0-3)^{2}} \\  \\ =\sqrt{16+9}=5 \\  \\ \therefore \text{Required shortest distance}=\dfrac{12}{5} \\  \\  \end{array}$

text: The mean and variance of a set of 15 numbers are 12 and 14 respectively. The mean and variance of another set of 15 numbers are 14 and $σ^{2}$ respectively. If the variance of all the 30 numbers in the two sets is 13 , then $σ^{2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know that if $n_{1},n_{2}$ are the sizes, $\bar{X}_{1},\bar{X}_{2}$ are the means and $σ_{1},σ_{2}$ are the standard deviation of the series, then the combine variance of the series.

$\begin{array}{ll}  & σ^{2}=\frac{n_{1}σ_{1}^{2}+n_{2}σ_{2}^{2}}{n_{1}+n_{2}}+\frac{n_{1}\cdot n_{2}}{(n_{1}+n_{2})^{2}}\left (\bar{X}_{1}-\bar{X}_{2}\right )^{2} \\  \\  & \Rightarrow 13=\frac{15\times 14+15\times σ^{2}}{15+15}+\frac{15\times 15}{(15+15)^{2}}(12-14)^{2} \\  \\  & \Rightarrow 13=\frac{14+σ^{2}}{2}+\frac{1}{4}\times 4 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow 14+σ^{2}=2\times 12 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow σ^{2}=10 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text: Let $\mathrm{A}=[\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{ij}}]_{2\times 2}$, where $\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{ij}}\neq 0$ for all $\mathrm{i},\mathrm{j}$ and $\mathrm{A}^{2}=\mathrm{I}$. Let a be the sum of all diagonal elements of $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{b}=|\mathrm{A}|$. Then $3a^{2}+4b^{2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $A^{2}=I$

and $b=|A|$

Let
$A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} a_{1} & b_{1} \\ a_{2} & b_{2} \end{array}\right ]$

$\begin{array}{llllll} \therefore A^{2} & =\left [\begin{array}{ll} a_{1} & b_{1} \\ a_{2} & b_{2} \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{ll} a_{1} & b_{1} \\ a_{2} & b_{2} \end{array}\right ] \\  \\ =\left [\begin{array}{ll} a_{1}^{2}+b_{1}a_{2} & a_{1}b_{1}+b_{1}b_{2} \\ a_{1}a_{2}+a_{2}b_{2} & b_{1}a_{2}+b_{2}^{2} \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]\left (\because A^{2}=I\right ) \end{array}$

By equality of matrices, we get

$\begin{array}{l} a_{1}a_{2}+a_{2}b_{2}=0\text{and}a_{1}b_{1}+b_{1}b_{2}=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow a_{2}(a_{1}+b_{2})=0\text{and}b_{1}(a_{1}+b_{2})=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow a_{1}+b_{2}=0\text{(since,}b_{1},a_{2}\neq 0\text{)} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \text{Sum of diagonal elements}=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow a=0 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Now,}A^{2}=I \\  \\ \Rightarrow \left |A^{2}\right |=1 \\  \\ \Rightarrow |A|^{2}=1(\because |A^{n}|=|A|^{n}) \\  \\ \Rightarrow b^{2}=1(\because |A|=b) \\  \\ \therefore 3a^{2}+4b^{2}=3(0)+4(1)=4 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text: Let $5f(x)+4f\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )=\frac{1}{x}+3,x>0$. Then $18\int\limits _{1}^{2}f(x)dx$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We have,

$5f(x)+4f\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )=\frac{1}{x}+3,x>0$ ..........(i)

On replacing $x$ by $\frac{1}{x}$ in (i), we get

$5f\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )+4f(x)=x+3$ ..........(ii)

Now, using Eq. (i) $\times 5-$ (ii) $\times 4$, we get

$\begin{array}{l} 25f(x)-16f(x)=\left (\dfrac{5}{x}+15\right )-(4x+12) \\  \\ \Rightarrow 9f(x)=\dfrac{5}{x}-4x+3 \\  \\ \Rightarrow f(x)=\dfrac{1}{9}\left (\dfrac{5}{x}-4x+3\right )...........(iii) \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \therefore  & 18\int\limits _{1}^{2}f(x)dx=18\int\limits _{1}^{2}\dfrac{1}{9}\left (\dfrac{5}{x}-4x+3\right )dx\text{[Using Eq. (iii)]} \\  \\ = & 2\int\limits _{1}^{2}\left (\dfrac{5}{x}-4x+3\right )dx \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} =2\left [5\log _{e}x-4\left (\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\right )+3x\right ]_{1}^{2} \\  \\ =2\left [\left (5\log _{e}2-2(2)^{2}+3(2)\right )-\left (5\log 1-2(1)^{2}+3(1)\right )\right ] \\  \\ =2[5\log _{e}2-8+6+2-3][\because \log 1=0] \\  \\ =10\log _{e}2-6 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text: Let $I(x)=\int \frac{x^{2}\left (x\sec ^{2}x+\tan x\right )}{(x\tan x+1)^{2}}dx$. If $I(0)=0$, then $I\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We have,

$\begin{array}{ll} I(x)= & \int \dfrac{x^{2}\left (x\sec ^{2}x+\tan x\right )}{(x\tan x+1)^{2}}dx \\  \\ = & x^{2}\int \dfrac{x\sec ^{2}x+\tan x}{(x\tan x+1)^{2}}dx \\  \\ -\int \left \{\dfrac{d}{dx}\left (x^{2}\right )\int \dfrac{x\sec ^{2}x+\tan x}{(x\tan x+1)^{2}}dx\right \}dx\text{(integration by parts)} \end{array}$

$=x^{2}\left (\frac{-1}{x\tan x+1}\right )+\int \frac{2x}{x\tan x+1}dx$

Now, let 

$\begin{array}{ll} I_{1} & =2\int \dfrac{x}{x\tan x+1}dx \\  \\ =2\int \dfrac{x\cos x}{x\sin x+\cos x}dx \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{On putting}x\sin x+\cos x=t \\  \\ \Rightarrow (x\cos x+\sin x-\sin x)dx=dt \\  \\ \Rightarrow x\cos xdx=dt \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore I_{1}=2\int \dfrac{dt}{t}=2\log t+c \\  \\ =2\log (x\sin x+\cos x)+c \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore I(x)=\dfrac{-x^{2}}{x\tan x+1}+2\log (x\sin x+\cos x)+c \end{array}$

When, $x=0$, then

$\begin{array}{ll}  & I(0)=0+2\log (1)+c=0 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow c=0 \\  \\  & \therefore I(x)=\frac{-x^{2}}{x\tan x+1}+2\log (x\sin x+\cos x) \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore I(x)=\dfrac{-x^{2}}{x\tan x+1}+2\log (x\sin x+\cos x) \\  \\ \Rightarrow I\left (\dfrac{π}{4}\right )=\dfrac{-\frac{π^{2}}{16}}{\frac{π}{4}+1}+2\log \left (\dfrac{π}{4}\times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right ) \\  \\ =\log \left (\dfrac{(π+4)^{2}}{32}\right )-\dfrac{π^{2}}{4(π+4)} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text:
Let $⃗{a}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k},⃗{b}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$ and $⃗{c}=-\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$.

If $⃗{d}$ is a vector perpendicular to both $⃗{b}$ and $⃗{c}$, and $⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{d}=18$, then $|⃗{a}\times ⃗{d}|^{2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A vector perpendicular to both $⃗{b}$ and $⃗{c}$ is parallel to $⃗{b}\times ⃗{c}$:

$⃗{b}\times ⃗{c}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & -2 & -2 \\ -1 & 4 & 3 \end{array}\right |=(-6+8)\hat{i}-(3-2)\hat{j}+(4-2)\hat{k}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$

So $⃗{d}=λ(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})$, and $⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{d}=λ(4-3+8)=9λ=18$ gives $λ=2$, i.e. $⃗{d}=4\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$.

$|⃗{a}|^{2}=4+9+16=29$ and $|⃗{d}|^{2}=16+4+16=36$.

By Lagrange's identity,

$|⃗{a}\times ⃗{d}|^{2}=|⃗{a}|^{2}|⃗{d}|^{2}-(⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{d})^{2}=29\times 36-18^{2}=1044-324=720$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text:
Let $a_{1},a_{2},a_{3},\ldots ,a_{\mathrm{n}}$ be $\mathrm{n}$ positive consecutive terms of an arithmetic progression. If $\mathrm{d}>0$ is its common difference, then

$\lim _{n\to \infty }\sqrt{\frac{d}{n}}\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{a_{1}}+\sqrt{a_{2}}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{a_{2}}+\sqrt{a_{3}}}+\ldots \ldots \ldots +\frac{1}{\sqrt{a_{n-1}}+\sqrt{a_{n}}}\right )$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{n\to \infty }\sqrt{\frac{d}{n}}\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{a_{1}}+\sqrt{a_{2}}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{a_{2}}+\sqrt{a_{3}}}+\ldots \ldots \ldots +\frac{1}{\sqrt{a_{n-1}}+\sqrt{a_{n}}}\right )$

Now, 

$\begin{array}{ll} \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a_{1}}+\sqrt{a_{2}}}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a_{2}}+\sqrt{a_{3}}}+\ldots +\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a_{n-1}}+\sqrt{a_{n}}} \\  \\ = & \dfrac{\sqrt{a_{2}}-\sqrt{a_{1}}}{a_{2}-a_{1}}+\dfrac{\sqrt{a_{3}}-\sqrt{a_{2}}}{a_{3}-a_{2}}+\ldots +\dfrac{\sqrt{a_{n}}-\sqrt{a_{n-1}}}{a_{n}-a_{n-1}} \\  \\ = & \dfrac{\sqrt{a_{2}}-\sqrt{a_{1}}+\sqrt{a_{3}}-\sqrt{a_{2}}+..+\sqrt{a_{n}}-\sqrt{a_{n-1}}}{d} \end{array}$

$(\because a_{2}-a_{1}=a_{3}-a_{2}=\ldots a_{n}-a_{n-1}=d)$

$\begin{array}{l} =\dfrac{\sqrt{a_{n}}-\sqrt{a_{1}}}{d} \\  \\ =\dfrac{\sqrt{a_{1}+(n-1)d}-\sqrt{a_{1}}}{d} \end{array}$

$\therefore \lim _{n\to \infty }\sqrt{\frac{d}{n}}\left (\frac{\sqrt{a_{1}+(n-1)d}-\sqrt{a_{1}}}{d}\right )$

$\begin{array}{l} =\lim _{n\to \infty }\left [\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\left (\dfrac{\sqrt{a_{1}+(n-1)d}-\sqrt{a_{1}}}{\sqrt{n}}\right )\right ] \\  \\ =\lim _{n\to \infty }\left [\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{d}}⎛⎝\sqrt{\dfrac{a_{1}}{n}+\left (d-\dfrac{d}{n}\right )}-\sqrt{\dfrac{a_{1}}{n}}⎞⎠\right ] \\  \\ =\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{d}}(\sqrt{0+d-0}-\sqrt{0})=\dfrac{\sqrt{d}}{\sqrt{d}}=1 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text: The sum of all the roots of the equation $\left |x^{2}-8x+15\right |-2x+7=0$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \text{We have,}\left |x^{2}-8x+15\right |-2x+7=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow |(x-3)(x-5)|-2x+7=0 \end{array}$


[IMG]


Now, when $x\leq 3$ or $x\geq 5$, then

$\begin{array}{ll}  & x^{2}-8x+15-2x+7=0 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow x^{2}-10x+22=0 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow x^{2}-10x+25-3=0 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow (x-5)^{2}-3=0 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow (x-5)=\pm \sqrt{3} \\  \\  & \Rightarrow x=5+\sqrt{3},5-\sqrt{3} \end{array}$

Since, $x\leq 3$ or $x\geq 5$

$\therefore x=5+\sqrt{3}$

When, $3<x<5$, then

$\begin{array}{ll}  & -\left (x^{2}-8x+15\right )-2x+7=0 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow -x^{2}+8x-15-2x+7=0 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow -x^{2}+6x-8=0 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow x^{2}-6x+8=0 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow (x-4)(x-2)=0\Rightarrow x=2,4 \end{array}$

Since, $3<x<5$

$\therefore x=4$

$\therefore \text{Sum of roots}=(5+\sqrt{3})+4=9+\sqrt{3}$

text: If the ratio of the fifth term from the beginning to the fifth term from the end in the expansion of $\left (\sqrt{4 2}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{4 3}}\right )^{\mathrm{n}}$ is $\sqrt{6}:1$, then the third term from the beginning is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{T}_{r+1}={}^{n}\mathrm{C}_{r}x^{n-r}a^{r}$

$\frac{T_{5}}{T_{5}^{'}}=\frac{{}^{n}C_{4}\times \left ((2)^{\dfrac{1}{4}}\right )^{n-4}\left (\frac{1}{3 1/4}\right )^{4}}{{}^{n}C_{4}\left (\frac{1}{3 1/4}\right )^{n-4}\left (2^{1/4}\right )^{4}}=\sqrt{6}$

$[\because r$th term from end in the expansion of $(x+y)^{n}=r$th term from beginning in the expansion of $(y+x)^{n}]$

$\Rightarrow \frac{{}^{n}C_{4}(2)^{\dfrac{n-4}{4}}\left (\frac{1}{3}\right )^{4/4}}{{}^{n}C_{4}\left (\frac{1}{3}\right )^{\dfrac{n-4}{4}}(2)^{4/4}}=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{1}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow (2)^{\frac{n-8}{4}}(3)^{\frac{n-8}{4}}=6^{1/2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow 6^{\frac{n-8}{4}}=6^{1/2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{n-8}{4}=\dfrac{1}{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow n-8=2\Rightarrow n=10 \end{array}$

$\therefore T_{3}={}^{10}C_{2}(\sqrt{4 2})^{8}\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{4 3}}\right )^{2}=45(2)^{\frac{8}{4}}\frac{1}{3^{1/2}}$

$=45(4)\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}=60\sqrt{3}$

text: If $2x^{y}+3y^{x}=20$, then $\frac{dy}{dx}$ at $(2,2)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $2x^{y}+3y^{x}=20$ ..........(i)

Let $u=x^{y}$

On taking log both sides, we get 

$\log u=y\log x$

On differentiating both sides with respect to $x$, we get

$\begin{array}{ll}  & \frac{1}{u}\frac{du}{dx}=y\frac{1}{x}+\log x\frac{dy}{dx} \\  \\  & \Rightarrow \frac{du}{dx}=u\left (\frac{y}{x}+\log x\frac{dy}{dx}\right ) \\  \\  & \Rightarrow \frac{du}{dx}=x^{y}\left (\frac{y}{x}+\log x\frac{dy}{dx}\right ).........(ii) \end{array}$

Also, let $v=y^{x}$ 

On taking log both sides, we get 

$\log v=x\log y$

On differentiating both sides, we get

$\begin{array}{ll}  & \frac{1}{v}\frac{dv}{dx}=x\frac{1}{y}\frac{dy}{dx}+\log y\cdot 1 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow \frac{dv}{dx}=v\left (\frac{x}{y}\frac{dy}{dx}+\log y\right ) \\  \\  & \Rightarrow \frac{dv}{dx}=y^{x}\left (\frac{x}{y}\frac{dy}{dx}+\log y\right )..........(iii) \end{array}$

Now, from Equation (i), $2u+3v=20$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow 2\dfrac{du}{dx}+3\dfrac{dv}{dx}=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 2x^{y}\left (\dfrac{y}{x}+\log x\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right )+3y^{x}\left (\dfrac{x}{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\log y\right )=0\text{[Using Eqs. (ii) and (iii)]} \end{array}$

On putting $x=2$ and $y=2$, we get

$\begin{array}{l} 2(4)\left (1+\log 2\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right )+3(4)\left (\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\log 2\right )=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx}(8\log 2+12)+(8+12\log 2)=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\left (\dfrac{2+3\log 2}{3+2\log 2}\right ) \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\left (\dfrac{2+\log 8}{3+\log 4}\right ) \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text: Let $y=y(x)$ be a solution of the differential equation $(x\cos x)dy+(xy\sin x+y\cos x-1)dx=0,0<x<\frac{π}{2}$. If $\frac{π}{3}y\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )=\sqrt{3}$, then $\left |\frac{π}{6}y^{''}\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )+2y^{'}\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )\right |$ is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Dividing by $x\cos x$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\left (\tan x+\dfrac{1}{x}\right )y=\dfrac{1}{x\cos x}$

The integrating factor is $e^{\int \left (\tan x+\frac{1}{x}\right )dx}=x\sec x$, so

$xy\sec x=\int \sec ^{2}xdx=\tan x+c$

At $x=\dfrac{π}{3}$, $xy=\sqrt{3}$: $\sqrt{3}\times 2=\sqrt{3}+c$, so $c=\sqrt{3}$.

Multiplying by $\cos x$: $xy=\sin x+\sqrt{3}\cos x$.

Differentiating twice:

$y+xy^{'}=\cos x-\sqrt{3}\sin x,2y^{'}+xy^{''}=-\sin x-\sqrt{3}\cos x$

At $x=\dfrac{π}{6}$:

$\dfrac{π}{6}\quad y^{''}\left (\dfrac{π}{6}\right )+2y^{'}\left (\dfrac{π}{6}\right )=-\dfrac{1}{2}-\sqrt{3}\cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=-2$

Its absolute value is $2$.

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text: If the area of the region $S=\left \{(x,y):2y-y^{2}\leq x^{2}\leq 2y,x\geq y\right \}$ is equal to $\frac{n+2}{n+1}-\frac{π}{n-1}$, then the natural number $n$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The condition $2y-y^{2}\leq x^{2}$ is $x^{2}+(y-1)^{2}\geq 1$: points on or outside the circle with centre $(0,1)$ and radius $1$. The condition $x^{2}\leq 2y$ means $y\geq \dfrac{x^{2}}{2}$.

The line $y=x$ meets the parabola $x^{2}=2y$ at $(0,0)$ and $(2,2)$, and meets the circle at $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$.

Inside the circle $x^{2}<2y-y^{2}\leq 2y$, so the whole disc lies above the parabola. Hence $S$ is the region between $y=\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}$ and $y=x$ for $0\leq x\leq 2$, minus the part of the disc below the line $y=x$.

$\int\limits _{0}^{2}\left (x-\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right )dx=2-\frac{4}{3}=\frac{2}{3}$

The radii to $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$ point along $(0,-1)$ and $(1,0)$, so the chord subtends a right angle at the centre; the centre lies above $y=x$, so the part of the disc below the line is the minor segment, of area $\dfrac{π(1)^{2}}{4}-\dfrac{1}{2}(1)(1)=\dfrac{π}{4}-\dfrac{1}{2}$.

$\text{Area of}S=\frac{2}{3}-\left (\frac{π}{4}-\frac{1}{2}\right )=\frac{7}{6}-\frac{π}{4}=\frac{5+2}{5+1}-\frac{π}{5-1}$

So $n=5$.

Hence, the answer is 5.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text: Let the point $(p,p+1)$ lie inside the region $E=\left \{(x,y):3-x\leq y\leq \sqrt{9-x^{2}},0\leq x\leq 3\right \}$. If the set of all values of $\mathrm{p}$ is the interval $(a,b)$, then $b^{2}+b-a^{2}$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given region,

$E=\left \{(x,y):3-x\leq y\leq \sqrt{9-x^{2}},0\leq x\leq 3\right \}$

Since, point $(p,p+1)$ lie on line $y=x+1$

$\therefore$ Point of intersection of $y=x+1$ and $y=3-x$

i.e.,
$x+1=3-x$

$\Rightarrow$ $2x=2\Rightarrow x=1$

and $y=2$

and point of intersection of $y=x+1$ and

$y=\sqrt{9-x^{2}}$

i.e., $(x+1)^{2}=9-x^{2}$

$\begin{array}{ll}  & \Rightarrow x^{2}+1+2x=9-x^{2} \\  \\  & \Rightarrow 2x^{2}+2x-8=0 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow x^{2}+x-4=0 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow x=\frac{-1\pm \sqrt{1+4(1)(4)}}{2} \\  \\  & \Rightarrow x=\frac{-1\pm \sqrt{17}}{2} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{lll} \Rightarrow  & x=\frac{-1+\sqrt{17}}{2}, & \text{(Since,}x\in [0,3]) \\  \\ \therefore  & p\in \left (1,\frac{-1+\sqrt{17}}{2}\right ) \end{array}$

$\Rightarrow a=1,b=\frac{-1+\sqrt{17}}{2}$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore b^{2}+b-a \\  \\ =\dfrac{1+17-2\sqrt{17}}{4}+\dfrac{(-1+\sqrt{17})}{2}-1 \\  \\ =\dfrac{18-2\sqrt{17}-2+2\sqrt{17}-4}{4} \\  \\ =\dfrac{12}{4}=3 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text: Let $a\in \mathrm{ℤ}$ and $[\mathrm{t}]$ be the greatest integer $\leq \mathrm{t}$. Then the number of points, where the function $f(x)=[a+13\sin x],x\in (0,π)$ is not differentiable, is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $a\in \mathrm{ℤ}$, $f(x)=[a+13\sin x]=a+[13\sin x]$, so $f$ fails to be differentiable exactly where $[13\sin x]$ does.

For $x\in (0,π)$, $13\sin x\in (0,13]$, and $[13\sin x]$ is locally constant wherever $13\sin x$ is not an integer.

For each $k=1,2,\ldots ,12$, $\sin x=\dfrac{k}{13}$ has two solutions in $(0,π)$, one on each side of $\dfrac{π}{2}$. At each of them $13\sin x$ crosses the integer $k$, so $[13\sin x]$ jumps between $k-1$ and $k$ and $f$ is discontinuous: $12\times 2=24$ points.

For $k=13$, $\sin x=1$ only at $x=\dfrac{π}{2}\in (0,π)$. There $f\left (\dfrac{π}{2}\right )=a+13$, while $f(x)=a+12$ for all nearby $x\neq \dfrac{π}{2}$, so $f$ is discontinuous and hence not differentiable at $x=\dfrac{π}{2}$.

Total number of points $=24+1=25$.

Hence, the answer is 25.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text: Let $\mathrm{A}=\{1,2,3,4,\ldots .,10\}$ and $\mathrm{B}=\{0,1,2,3,4\}$. The number of elements in the relation $R=\left \{(a,b)\in A\times A:2(a-b)^{2}+3(a-b)\in B\right \}$ is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given sets :

A={1,2,3,4, ............,10}

 B={0,1,2,3,4}

We are looking for pairs $(a,b)\in A\times A$ such that :

$2(a-b)^{2}+3(a-b)\in B$

Let's break down the relation :

Case 1 : $a-b=0$

$2(a-b)^{2}+3(a-b)=0$

Pairs : $(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),\ldots ,(10,10)$ which gives 10 pairs.

Case 2 : $a-b=1$

$2(a-b)^{2}+3(a-b)=2(1)+3(1)=5$

But 5 is not in B, so no pairs for this case.

Case 3 : $a-b=-1$

$2(a-b)^{2}+3(a-b)=2(1)-3(1)=-1$

This value is not in B, so no pairs for this case.

Case 4 : $a-b=2$

$2(a-b)^{2}+3(a-b)=2(4)+3(2)=8+6=14$

Again, 14 is not in B, so no pairs for this case.

Case 5 : $a-b=-2$

$2(a-b)^{2}+3(a-b)=2(4)-3(2)=8-6=2$

Pairs : $(1,3),(2,4),(3,5),(4,6),(5,7),(6,8),(7,9),(8,10)$ which gives 8 pairs.

For any other $a-b$ value, the quadratic will grow larger than the maximum value in B, so we don't need to consider them.

In total, we have $10+8=18$ pairs in the relation $R$.

Therefore, the number of elements in the relation $R$ is 18.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text:
A circle passing through the point $P(α,β)$ in the first quadrant touches the two coordinate axes at the points $A$ and $B$. The point $P$ is above the line $AB$. The point $Q$ on the line segment $AB$ is the foot of perpendicular from $P$ on $AB$. If $PQ$ is equal to 11 units, then the value of $αβ$ is
 $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The circle touches both axes in the first quadrant, so its centre is $(a,a)$, its radius is $a$, and it touches the axes at $A(a,0)$ and $B(0,a)$:

$(x-a)^{2}+(y-a)^{2}=a^{2}.$


[IMG]

$P(α,β)$ lies on it:

$α^{2}+β^{2}-2aα-2aβ+a^{2}=0\text{...(i)}$

Line $AB$ is $x+y=a$. $P$ is above $AB$, so $α+β-a>0$ and

$PQ=\frac{α+β-a}{\sqrt{2}}=11\Rightarrow (α+β-a)^{2}=242.$

Expanding,

$α^{2}+β^{2}+a^{2}-2aα-2aβ+2αβ=242.$

Using (i), $2αβ=242\Rightarrow αβ=121$.

Hence, the answer is 121.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text: The number of ways of giving 20 distinct oranges to 3 children such that each child gets at least one orange is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Total ways without any restrictions :

There are $3^{20}$ ways to distribute the oranges to the 3 children.

Number of ways one child receives no orange :

Choose 1 child out of the 3 to not receive any orange in ${}^{3}C_{1}=3$ ways. Distribute 20 oranges to the remaining 2 children in $2^{20}$ ways. However, we've included the scenarios where the 2 children each get all the oranges. So, we subtract the 2 ways where one of the two remaining children gets all the oranges.
${}^{3}C_{1}(2^{20}-2)$

Number of ways two children receive no orange :

Choose 2 children out of the 3 to not receive any oranges in ${}^{3}C_{2}=3$ ways. The third child will receive all 20 oranges in $1^{20}=1$ way.
${}^{3}C_{2}\times 1^{20}=3$

Number of ways 

$=$ Total $-($ One child receive no orange + two child receive no orange)

$\begin{array}{l} =3^{20}-\left ({}^{3}C_{1}\left (2^{20}-2\right )+{}^{3}C_{2}1^{20}\right ) \\  \\ =3483638676 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift
